title: Martin de Porres (1579–1639)
hook: a mixed-race Dominican brother in Lima, with a broom, a clinic, and mice he fed

segments.voice: Yesterday, Rose of Lima in her garden hut, nursing the sick in her parents' house, a Dominican tertiary. Your line was first of the americas. Did you hold a place in Latin America for a breath? Today we stay in the same city. Day eight hundred fifty-nine.

A statue of him will often show the same things: a Dominican in a black and white habit, a dark-skinned face, and in his hand, not a book or a sword, but a broom. Sometimes there's a dog at his feet, a cat, and a mouse, all eating from one bowl. It looks like a children's picture. It's actually a summary of a life. He swept floors, cut hair, set bones, fed the hungry at the door, and for a long time held the lowest place in his house. Today, Martin de Porres.
screen: `NOT A BOOK, NOT A SWORD.` → `A BROOM.` → `A DOG, A CAT, A MOUSE.`

segments.voice: First, where he started. Martin was born in Lima, the son of a Spanish nobleman and a freed Black woman. His father did not acknowledge him at first. The colonial world sorted people by race, and Martin landed near the bottom. Second, the door that was half open. He trained as a barber, which in his day also meant small surgery and setting bones. Then he asked to join the Dominicans. The rules of the time kept men like him from taking full vows, so he entered as a donado, a lay helper who gave his work to the house. He swept. He cleaned. Only later did the community admit him as a professed brother. Third, the clinic. He became the infirmarian, caring for sick friars, and the care spread out the door: to slaves, to the poor of the city, to anyone who came. Fourth, the stories. Tradition says that when the priory was short of money, Martin offered to be sold to pay its debts. Tradition says he struck a deal with the mice in the house: stay in the garden, and I'll feed you there. Some of these are legends, retold many times; even so, they point one way. He took the lowest place and made it holy. Jesus describes himself in that place, in the Douay-Rheims: "I am in the midst of you, as he that serveth." The broom in his statues is not decoration. It's the claim his life makes: that sweeping a floor for God is not a lesser kind of prayer.
screen: `A NOBLEMAN'S SON, NOT ACKNOWLEDGED.` · `A DONADO: THE LOWEST PLACE.` · `THE CLINIC OUT THE DOOR.` · `SELL ME. FEED THE MICE.` · then, large: `AS HE THAT SERVETH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: do a humble job gladly. Settle, and breathe. Think of one small chore waiting for you today, the kind nobody thanks anyone for. Dishes, a trash bag, a floor, an inbox. Picture yourself doing it, slowly, without hurrying to be done. Notice whether something in you says this is beneath me. Let that voice speak, then let it pass. If you pray, you can offer the chore to God before you start. If you don't, simply decide to do it well. The bell holds the time.
Donado. A lay helper who gives his work to the house without taking full vows, the place Martin de Porres entered before the community made him a professed brother.
Your line: the saint with a broom. Today, pick up one job someone else would skip, and do it as if it mattered, because to someone it does. Day eight hundred fifty-nine.

howItsDone: Catholics often show Saint Martin de Porres with a broom, and some parishes and schools named for him run food pantries or outreach to the poor; he is invoked by people who face racial prejudice.

notes: Editor pass: 'the lowest-ranked man in his house for years' softened to 'for a long time held the lowest place in his house'; removed a stray blank line in these notes.

Claims rule: no dates or counts in the voice. Confirm: father a Spanish nobleman (Juan de Porres), mother a freed Black woman (Ana Velázquez); father did not acknowledge him at first; entry as a donado because of rules on race; later profession as a brother.
'Tradition says' the offer to be sold and the deal with the mice; the fork reveal says the community did not accept the offer. Confirm.
'The lowest-ranked man in his house for years' is an interpretation of donado status; confirm.
Second editor: the 'whether or not every story happened' turn repeated day 852's device; reworded.
